package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is designed to covertly surveil victims by exfiltrating SMS (including 2FA codes), recording audio, stealing contacts and account data, and forwarding sensitive information to attacker-controlled infrastructure. It masquerades as a legitimate service but performs extensive unauthorized data collection and exfiltration.

execution_context.file_location: Android app main service (background receiver for SMS events)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code intercepts incoming SMS messages, extracts their content, and forwards them to a phone number controlled by the attacker, enabling real-time exfiltration of 2FA codes and other sensitive messages.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and forwarding all SMS messages, especially 2FA codes, to an external number is a clear sign of credential theft and surveillance.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate app should not forward private SMS messages to third parties without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parental control or enterprise monitoring apps may intercept SMS, but with user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: Forwards SMS content to hardcoded external number
Requires broad SMS and network permissions

execution_context.file_location: Android app background service (audio recording module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a command from the C2 server, the code activates the device microphone, records ambient audio, saves it to a file, and uploads the recording to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Covertly recording audio and exfiltrating it is a hallmark of spyware and surveillance malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps must request explicit user permission and provide clear indication when recording audio.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Voice memo or call recording apps, but only with user consent and notification.
key_indicators: Background audio recording without user interaction
Automatic upload of recordings to remote server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on command from C2 or at startup)
execution_context.file_location: Android app background service (contacts and accounts exfiltration module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects all contacts and account information from the device and sends this data to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting all contacts and account data without user knowledge is a privacy violation and enables further social engineering or credential attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only access contacts/accounts for core functionality and with user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Contact backup or sync apps, but with user opt-in and clear privacy policy.
key_indicators: Bulk exfiltration of contacts and accounts

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on command from C2 or at scheduled intervals)
execution_context.file_location: Android app background service (device info and app/process enumeration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates all installed applications and running processes, then sends this inventory to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Enumerating installed apps and running processes is often used for reconnaissance and to tailor further attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not need to inventory all apps/processes unless for device management or security purposes, and should inform the user.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device management or antivirus apps, but with user awareness.

execution_context.file_location: Android app activity (Google account phishing screen)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<WebView ...>
  loadUrl('https://malicious-phishing-site.com/google-login')
</WebView>
// Collect credentials entered and send to C2
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app presents a fake Google login page in a WebView, collects user credentials, and sends them to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Presenting a fake login page to steal credentials is a classic phishing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should redirect to official OAuth flows, not embed fake login forms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; credential phishing is always malicious.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the malicious Android app, believing it to be a legitimate service.
attack_chain.leads_to: App requests and obtains broad permissions.

attack_chain.action: App requests permissions for SMS, contacts, audio recording, and more.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is able to access sensitive data and device features.

attack_chain.action: App intercepts incoming SMS messages and forwards them to attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives 2FA codes and other sensitive SMS.

attack_chain.action: App records ambient audio on command and uploads it to attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's surroundings.

attack_chain.action: App exfiltrates contacts and account information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can perform social engineering or further attacks.

attack_chain.action: App enumerates installed apps and running processes, sending data to attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can tailor further attacks or evade detection.

attack_chain.action: App presents phishing UI to steal Google account credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains credentials for further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Background interception and forwarding of SMS messages to external numbers
Covert audio recording and network exfiltration of recordings
Bulk exfiltration of contacts, accounts, and device inventory
Presentation of phishing UIs for credential theft
file_indicators: Android APKs requesting excessive permissions (SMS, audio, contacts, accounts)
Presence of code for SMS interception and forwarding
Embedded WebView loading non-official login pages
network_indicators: Outbound SMS to unknown international numbers
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled C2 domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android apps requesting broad permissions unrelated to their stated function, especially those intercepting and forwarding SMS or recording audio in the background. Analyze network traffic for suspicious outbound SMS or data exfiltration to untrusted domains. Detect embedded WebViews loading login pages not associated with official providers. Use mobile security solutions to flag apps with these behaviors and cross-reference with known IOCs.
